title: Polynomial alternating differential of a parametrized pencil
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a smooth projective geometrically integral finite-type $F$-scheme of dimension one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-kun-projective, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], put $\omega=\Omega^1_{C/F}$ with its universal derivation $d$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and put $J=\Gamma(C,M)$ and $Q=\Gamma(C,\omega\otimes M^{\otimes2})$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $\omega$ is invertible and $J,Q$ are finite-dimensional $F$-vector spaces. The formula
$$\delta(s,t)=(\beta\,d\alpha-\alpha\,d\beta)e^{\otimes2},\qquad s=\alpha e,\quad t=\beta e,$$
in a local frame $e$ of $M$ is independent of that frame and defines an $F$-bilinear alternating map $\delta:J\times J\to Q$. Let $P=\mathbf A^m_F$ for any finite $m\geq0$, and let $s_P,t_P$ be sections of the pullback of $M$ to $C\times_FP$ whose coordinates under the canonical identification with $J\otimes_F F[P]$ are polynomials on $P$. There is a polynomial map $\Delta:P\to\mathbf A(Q)$ with $\Delta(v)=\delta(s_v,t_v)$ after every extension field $E/F$; here $\mathbf A(Q)$ is the affine space associated to $Q$. More precisely for every commutative $F$-algebra $R$ one has the canonical isomorphisms $\omega_R\simeq\Omega^1_{C_R/R}$ and $Q\otimes_FR\simeq\Gamma(C_R,\Omega^1_{C_R/R}\otimes M_R^{\otimes2})$, taking $1\otimes df$ to $d(1\otimes f)$ and the pullback of $\delta$ to the same local formula over $R$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-module-pullback]. Thus the formula over the coordinate ring $F[P]$ and its specialization agree. In any basis of $Q$, the finitely many coordinate polynomials of $\Delta$ cut out a closed zero locus; its open complement $D_\Delta$ satisfies $v\in D_\Delta(E)$ exactly when $\delta(s_v,t_v)\ne0$.

proof.text: The structure morphism of $C$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. The field $F$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $F$. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is Noetherian and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. These facts supply the properness and Noetherian hypotheses for coherent cohomology below.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; projective properness as in the cited blueprint lemma

proof.text: Since $C$ is integral of dimension one, its sole irreducible component has dimension one. Its sole fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is therefore equidimensional of dimension one; the smooth-relative-dimension convention of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] gives relative dimension one. Apply [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free] with $d=1$: $\omega$ is locally free of rank one, hence invertible. In local frames $M$ and $\omega\otimes M^{\otimes2}$ are each $\mathcal O_C$. Thus both are quasi-coherent of finite type, by the definitions of invertibility and sheaf tensor product. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] both are coherent on the Noetherian $C$. Apply [lem-pc-coherent-hi] with base $\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $i=0$ to each: $J$ and $Q$ are finite $F$-modules, equivalently finite-dimensional vector spaces.

proof.text:
Use the affine-local differential sheaf [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. On an open with frame $e$ write $s=\alpha e,t=\beta e$ and set $w_e=(\beta\,d\alpha-\alpha\,d\beta)e^{\otimes2}$. For another frame $e'=ue$, with $u$ a unit, the coefficients become $u^{-1}\alpha,u^{-1}\beta$. The derivation rules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] give
$$d(u^{-1}\alpha)=u^{-1}d\alpha-u^{-2}\alpha\,du,$$
and likewise for $\beta$. Consequently
$$(u^{-1}\beta)d(u^{-1}\alpha)-(u^{-1}\alpha)d(u^{-1}\beta)=u^{-2}(\beta\,d\alpha-\alpha\,d\beta).$$
Multiplication by $(e')^{\otimes2}=u^2e^{\otimes2}$ cancels this factor. The expressions agree on intersections and under restriction, so the sheaf gluing axiom gives a unique section $\delta(s,t)$ of $\omega\otimes M^{\otimes2}$.

source.place: Tag 07BK, definition-differentials, derivation rules; agent frame-change cancellation

proof.text: The same local formula is additive separately in $\alpha$ and $\beta$. For $a\in F$ the universal derivation has $da=0$, so $d(a\alpha)=a\,d\alpha$, and $w_e(a\alpha,\beta)=a\,w_e(\alpha,\beta)=w_e(\alpha,a\beta)$. Finally $w_e(\alpha,\alpha)=0$ by cancellation of its two identical terms. Equality of sections is local, so $\delta$ is $F$-bilinear and alternating, including in characteristic two.

source.place: Tag 07BK, definition-differentials; agent bilinearity and alternatingness calculation

proof.text: Fix any commutative $F$-algebra $R$ and let $p_R:C_R\to C$ be the projection. Apply [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}F$: the canonical map $c:p_R^*\omega\to\Omega^1_{C_R/R}$, characterized locally by $1\otimes df\mapsto d(p_R^\sharp f)$, is an isomorphism $\omega_R\simeq\Omega^1_{C_R/R}$. On $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset C$ it is the map $(R\otimes_FA)\otimes_A\Omega_{A/F}\to\Omega_{R\otimes_FA/R}$, $b\otimes df\mapsto b\,d(1\otimes f)$, of [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], and these agree on overlaps (the statement of that node; no affine intersection is assumed). The pullback and tensor definitions identify $p_R^*(\omega\otimes M^{\otimes2})$ with $\omega_R\otimes M_R^{\otimes2}$: on an open with frame $e$ of $M$ both sides are $p_R^*\omega$, locally $\eta\otimes e^{\otimes2}\mapsto p_R^*\eta\otimes e_R^{\otimes2}$, and a frame change $e'=ue$ multiplies both sides by $u^2$, resp. $(p_R^\sharp u)^2$. Since $c(1\otimes d\alpha)=d(p_R^\sharp\alpha)$, pulling back $w_e(\alpha,\beta)$ gives exactly the relative formula $w_{e_R}(p_R^\sharp\alpha,p_R^\sharp\beta)$; by Step 3 these glue, so $p_R^*\delta(s,t)$ is the relative formula on $p_R^*s,p_R^*t$. For an $F$-algebra map $R\to R'$ the composite of the canonical maps for $R$ and $R\to R'$ sends $1\otimes df$ to $d(1\otimes f)$, hence is the canonical map for $R'$.

proof.text:
Every $F$-algebra $R$ is flat over $F$: every exact sequence of vector spaces splits, and its tensor product remains split exact. The structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is proper (Step 1), hence of finite type, so quasi-compact, and separated, hence quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to the cartesian square of $C_R=C\times_F\operatorname{Spec}R$, with $g:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ flat, $i=0$, and the quasi-coherent sheaves $M$ and $\omega\otimes M^{\otimes2}$ (equivalently [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent] with $k=F,k'=R$). The base change map is an isomorphism; on global sections over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ in degree $0$ it is the map $s\otimes r\mapsto r\,p_R^*s$, adjunction unit of $p_R^*$ followed by the $R$-module structure. This gives the canonical isomorphisms
$$J\otimes_FR\simeq\Gamma(C_R,M_R),\qquad Q\otimes_FR\simeq\Gamma(C_R,\Omega^1_{C_R/R}\otimes M_R^{\otimes2}),$$
using Step 5 for the second target. For $r,r'\in R$, the relative derivation kills $r,r'$, hence the local formula on $r\,p_R^*s,r'\,p_R^*t$ is $rr'\,p_R^*\delta(s,t)$. Additivity extends this identity to all finite sums of pure tensors. Thus, under these canonical isomorphisms, the formula over $R$ is precisely the scalar extension of the bilinear map $\delta$; since pullbacks compose, $p_{R'}^*=q^*p_R^*$ for $q:C_{R'}\to C_R$, and this identity commutes with maps $R\to R'$.

proof.text:
Choose bases $u_1,\ldots,u_N$ of $J$ and $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ of $Q$, allowing either basis to be empty. Write $\delta(u_i,u_j)=\sum_k c_{kij}q_k$, with $c_{kij}\in F$. Put $B=F[P]=F[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ and write the given sections as $s_P=\sum_i a_i u_i,t_P=\sum_j b_j u_j$ with $a_i,b_j\in B$ under Step 6. That step identifies their relative differential with
$$\sum_{k=1}^r h_kq_k,\qquad h_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^N c_{kij}a_i b_j\in B.$$
Under the basis identification $\mathbf A(Q)=\mathbf A^r_F$, the ring homomorphism $F[y_1,\ldots,y_r]\to B$, $y_k\mapsto h_k$, defines the required polynomial map $\Delta$ by [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-affine-space]. A change of either basis transforms this coordinate expression by the corresponding invertible linear matrix; it represents the same $Q\otimes_FB$ element and hence the same map to $\mathbf A(Q)$. For every $F$-algebra map $v:B\to R$, applying $v$ to the displayed finite sums gives the relative formula on $s_v,t_v$ by Step 6. In particular this is $\Delta(v)=\delta(s_v,t_v)$ over every extension field $E/F$.

source.place: Definition of affine space and the agent finite-coordinate expansion of the local differential formula

proof.text: Let $I=(h_1,\ldots,h_r)\subset B$. By the Zariski topology on the affine spectrum, $V(I)$ is closed; its complement is $D_\Delta=\bigcup_kD(h_k)$. An $E$-point $v$ lies there precisely when some $h_k(v)$ is nonzero, precisely when $\sum_k h_k(v)q_k$ is nonzero in $Q\otimes_FE$, since the $q_k$ remain a basis. By Step 7 this is $\delta(s_v,t_v)\ne0$. The ideal and zero locus are independent of the basis of $Q$: an invertible linear coordinate change replaces the list of generators by invertible linear combinations. If $r=0$ or all $h_k$ vanish, $I=0$ and $D_\Delta$ is empty, as required. If $m=0$, all formulas hold in $B=F$.
